:::{#def-secant-condition}
#### Secant condition

Let $f : \reals^p \to \reals$ have first [partial derivatives](vector-calculus.qmd#def-partial-derivative),
and let $\vx, \vx^+ \in \reals^p$.
Write $\vecf{s} \eqdef \vx^+ - \vx$ for the step
and $\vy \eqdef \deriv{\vx} f(\vx^+) - \deriv{\vx} f(\vx)$ for the change in the [gradient](vector-calculus.qmd#def-vector-derivative).
A [symmetric matrix](linear-algebra.qmd#def-symmetric-matrix) $\matr{B}$ satisfies the **secant condition**
[@nocedal2006numerical, Chapter 6]
for $(\vecf{s}, \vy)$ when

$$
\matr{B} \vecf{s} = \vy.
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-secant-condition}
#### The Hessian of a quadratic function satisfies the secant condition

Let $f(\vx) = \tfrac{1}{2} \qform{\matr{Q}}{\vx} - \dprod{\vecf{b}}{\vx}$
with $\matr{Q}$ [symmetric](linear-algebra.qmd#def-symmetric-matrix).
Then $\deriv{\vx} f(\vx) = \matr{Q} \vx - \vecf{b}$,
so for any $\vx$ and $\vx^+$

$$
\ba
\vy
&= (\matr{Q} \vx^+ - \vecf{b}) - (\matr{Q} \vx - \vecf{b})
&& \text{(gradient at each point)}
\\
&= \matr{Q} (\vx^+ - \vx)
&& \text{(collect terms)}
\\
&= \matr{Q} \vecf{s}.
&& \text{(definition of } \vecf{s} \text{)}
\ea
$$

So the Hessian $\matr{Q}$ of the [quadratic function](algebra-exponentials.qmd#def-quadratic-polynomial) satisfies the secant condition for every step.
For a general $f$, $\vy \approx \matr{H}_f \vecf{s}$ holds for a short step, with $\matr{H}_f$ the Hessian of $f$ near the step,
which is why a [matrix](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-matrix) that satisfies the secant condition is a reasonable stand-in for the Hessian.

:::
